title: World Youth Championships day five preview: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi open the U19 singles in Istanbul
seo_title: World Youth Championships day 5 preview and UK times
description: World Youth Championships day five: the U19 boys' and girls' singles last 32 in Istanbul, with Wen Ruibo, Jiang Yiyi, Hana Goda and Emanuel Otalvaro, in UK time.
standfirst: The under-19 singles begin on Wednesday with 32 matches from midday UK time, and four Chinese players who already have team gold are still chasing four titles each.
body: The under-19 singles, the last two under-19 titles to start at the World Youth Championships in Istanbul, begin on Wednesday with the boys' and girls' last 32. The top seeds, China's Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi, are on the first tables at midday UK time.

There are 32 matches in eight sessions, four at a time, from midday until about 5.15pm UK time. China have four players in the two draws, and all four, Wen, Jiang, Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan, are still in contention for four gold medals each after winning the team titles on Monday and reaching the finals or semi-finals of both doubles events.
## The big matches
**Wen Ruibo v Danilo Faso (12pm UK)**

Wen, 19, is the world No 14 and the highest-ranked player in Istanbul. He won both his singles in [China's 3-1 win over Taiwan in the boys' team final](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-u19-team-finals-china-beat-taiwan-japan.html), plays Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan in the all-Chinese mixed doubles final on Thursday and partners Li in the boys' doubles semi-finals. He has also qualified for the WTT Finals in Hong Kong next month. Faso, 16, is ranked 218th. The winner meets Ramon Vila of the Dominican Republic or Puerto Rico's Steven Moreno in the last 16.
**Mak Ming Shum v Hana Goda (2.15pm UK)**

Egypt's Goda, 18, is the world No 21 and the highest-ranked woman in the draws, but she is seeded third behind Jiang and Japan's Mao Takamori. Her doubles have gone badly this week: she and Romania's Bianca Mei-Rosu won the first game against Takamori and Aoba Takahashi but lost 3-1 in the girls' doubles last 16, and she and Kazakhstan's Alan Kurmangaliyev went out of the mixed doubles in the last 32. Mak, 17, is ranked 373rd and plays the doubles for Hong Kong with Su Tsz Tung.
**Sally Moyland v Syndrela Das (4.30pm UK)**

The only first-round match between two players in the world top 100. Moyland, 19, of the United States is ranked 77th and seeded seventh; India's Das, 17, is 95th. Das and Priyanuj Bhattacharyya took Li and Yao to a deciding game in the mixed doubles last 16 before losing 11-6 in the fifth.
**Kohaku Nakano v Emanuel Otalvaro (5.15pm UK)**

Otalvaro, the second seed, is 16 and ranked 106th. This month he won the boys' singles silver at the Youth Olympic Games, beating Li Hechen in the quarter-finals in Dakar, [the result that left China without a table tennis medal at the Games for the first time](/news/youth-olympic-games-dakar-2026-otalvaro-beats-li-hechen-china-no-medal.html), before losing the final 4-2 to Japan's Ryusei Kawakami. Nakano, 17, won a mixed doubles bronze on Tuesday with Takahashi. Otalvaro and Li, the sixth seed, are in the same quarter of the draw and could meet again in the quarter-finals.
## Jiang and the girls' draw

Jiang, who turned 16 last week, won four singles out of four in the team semi-final and final, including a 11-5, 11-9, 12-10 win over Takamori that finished the final. She opens against Lilian Ma of the United States, ranked 435th. Takamori, 18, the second seed, beat Yao in the team final and plays Poland's Karolina Holda in the last match of the day; she and Yao, seeded sixth and drawn against Austria's Nina Skerbinz, are in the same half and could meet in the semi-finals.

Hong Kong's Su Tsz Tung, ranked 57th and seeded fourth, plays Portugal's Julia Leal at 3pm. Australia's Constantina Psihogios, ranked 67th, plays South Africa's Rochica Sonday at 5.15pm, and India's Divyanshi Bhowmick, ranked 100th and seeded eighth, plays Russia's Zlata Terekhova at 1.30pm.
## Taiwan and the boys' seeds

Hung Che-Yen, 17, who beat Li Hechen in the team final and took Wen to a deciding game in the decisive match, plays Poland's Patryk Zyworonek at 12.45pm, in Wen's quarter of the draw. Taiwan's Lin Chin-Ting, the seventh seed, plays Australia's Aditya Sareen, ranked 112th, at 3.45pm. Kurmangaliyev, the third seed and the world No 131, and his doubles partner, Iran's Benyamin Faraji, the fifth seed, both play their first singles before they meet South Korea's Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho in Thursday's doubles semi-finals. Kim plays Japan's Shunto Iwaida at 1.30pm.
France's Antoine Noirault and Nathan Pilard, who meet Wen and Li in the doubles semi-finals, play Slovakia's Samuel Arpas and India's eighth seed, Abhinandh Pradhivadhi, respectively.
## Order of play
Times are approximate and UK time (Istanbul is three hours ahead). Seeds in brackets.

- 12pm: Wen Ruibo (CHN, 1) v Danilo Faso (ITA); Ramon Vila (DOM) v Steven Moreno (PUR); Jiang Yiyi (CHN, 1) v Lilian Ma (USA); Aybuke Simsek (TUR) v Alexia Nodin (FRA)
- 12.45pm: Hung Che-Yen (TPE) v Patryk Zyworonek (POL); Kenan Kahraman (TUR) v Benyamin Faraji (IRI, 5); Bianca Mei-Rosu (ROU) v Tania Morice (ALG); Tracey Hsia (NZL) v Wu Ying Syuan (TPE, 5)
- 1.30pm: Abhinandh Pradhivadhi (IND, 8) v Nathan Pilard (FRA); Kim Daehwan (KOR) v Shunto Iwaida (JPN); Divyanshi Bhowmick (IND, 8) v Zlata Terekhova (RUS); Natalia Bogdanowicz (POL) v Koharu Itagaki (GER)
- 2.15pm: Ivan Kahn (NED) v Wassim Essid (TUN); Chulong Nie (AUS) v Alan Kurmangaliyev (KAZ, 3); Aoba Takahashi (JPN) v Heo Yerim (KOR); Mak Ming Shum (HKG) v Hana Goda (EGY, 3)
- 3pm: Li Ki Ho (HKG, 4) v Berk Oztoprak (TUR); Antoine Noirault (FRA) v Samuel Arpas (SVK); Su Tsz Tung (HKG, 4) v Julia Leal (POR); Maria Berzosa (ESP) v Leana Hochart (FRA)
- 3.45pm: Samuel Michna (POL) v Lee Hyeonho (KOR); Aditya Sareen (AUS) v Lin Chin-Ting (TPE, 7); Jeong Yein (KOR) v Eseniia Shirokova (RUS); Nina Skerbinz (AUT) v Yao Ruixuan (CHN, 6)
- 4.30pm: Li Hechen (CHN, 6) v Yassin Gaber (EGY); Robert Istrate (ROU) v Francesco Trevisan (ITA); Sally Moyland (USA, 7) v Syndrela Das (IND); Busra Demir (TUR) v Wu Jia-En (TPE)
- 5.15pm: Priyanuj Bhattacharyya (IND) v Enrique Rios (PUR); Kohaku Nakano (JPN) v Emanuel Otalvaro (COL, 2); Constantina Psihogios (AUS) v Rochica Sonday (RSA); Karolina Holda (POL) v Mao Takamori (JPN, 2)
## How to watch

Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches) has live scores, the full draws and the order of play, and shows the stream whenever one is live. The times of the last 16 had not been published by early on Wednesday. On Thursday the boys' and girls' doubles semi-finals start at about 2.30pm UK time and the U19 mixed doubles final follows at about 5pm.
## Tuesday in brief

Both Chinese mixed doubles pairs beat Japanese opponents in the semi-finals, so China are guaranteed that title, and Wen and Li reached the boys' doubles semi-finals by beating Iwaida and Nakano 11-9, 11-6, 11-4. In the girls' doubles, Jiang and Yao came from a game down to beat Russia's Zlata Terekhova and Eseniia Shirokova, and France's Leana Hochart and Alexia Nodin beat Hong Kong's Su and Mak 11-9 in the fifth game. The details are in Eleven's [mixed doubles semi-final report](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-u19-mixed-doubles-semi-finals-all-china-final.html).
